name: X (Twitter)
refreshNote: No official cache-busting tool any more. The Card Validator (cards-dev.x.com/validator) no longer renders previews; X says to preview by pasting the URL into the post composer. Changing the URL (e.g. adding a query string) forces a fresh fetch; X does not publish its cache TTL.
notes: X developer docs (Cards markup): twitter:title max 70 chars, twitter:description max 200 chars, twitter:image:alt max 420 chars; twitter:title/description/image fall back to og:title/og:description/og:image. The 70/200 values are documented maxima, not measured on-screen truncation.

summary_large_image: min 300x157, recommended 1200x628, cropped to 2:1 (per docs/search extracts; some secondary guides quote 1.91:1). Images must be < 5MB; JPG, PNG, WEBP, GIF supported, only the first frame of an animated GIF is used; SVG not supported.

summary card (the documented default): square thumbnail, min 144x144, max 4096x4096, 5MB, cropped 1:1 (secondary sources). A mock should switch to a small square thumbnail when twitter:card is 'summary' or missing.

Behaviour change: in Oct 2023 X removed headline and description from link cards (image + domain overlay only). From late Nov 2023 / Jan 2024 X began overlaying the title as small white text on a dark box at the bottom-left of the image; secondary reporting (2025) says organic posts still show the headline over the image with no description panel. Domain is shown ('From example.com' below / overlay on the image).
Description is not shown on large-image cards in the timeline; whether the summary (small-thumbnail) layout shows the description varies by client - treat as uncertain.
twitter:card has no OG fallback; without it X may still render a card from OG tags, but layout defaults to summary (secondary sources).
twitter:image:alt is used for accessibility only (not rendered visibly).

Verification method: official doc pages were located via web search (search-engine extracts of the official URLs listed in source); direct page fetches of the official domain were blocked from the research environment, so wording could not be re-read in full.
